title: Intent Lab: 7-week Retrospective & KPI Fold
content:
Context:
This doc is my loose notebook for a 7-week personal sprint ("Intent Lab") focused on improving my contribution throughput and async impact at Redwood. Not a polished OKR — just working hypotheses, quick metrics, and experiment notes. Use this as a single source for weekly check-ins and a retrospective when I close the loop.

Primary hypothesis:
If I structure weekly micro-goals tied to measurable throughput signals and eliminate two recurring time-sinks, my effective contribution (measurable diff in PRs/knowledge-sharing/mentoring) rises by ~30% over 7 weeks.

High-level objective (north star):
- Increase "effective contribution" index by 30% by end of 7 weeks. Effective contribution = normalized combo of merged PRs, paired reviews, docs authored, and mentorship minutes. (I know it's fuzzy — it'll do for now).

Key metrics (baseline -> target):
- Merged PRs/week: 0.8 -> 1.4
- Review turnaround (avg hours): 48h -> 24h
- Docs authored (useful internal): 0.2 -> 0.6 per week
- Mentorship minutes logged: 25 -> 60 per week
- Deep focus hours/week (>=90m blocks): 6 -> 12

Tracking approach:
- Weekly snapshot every Friday morning. Quick numbers and 1-sentence signal.
- Use simple spreadsheet (sheet linked above) but keep this doc as narrative.

Week-by-week quick log:
Week 1 (11/03): baseline, messy schedule. Did quick inbox triage, blocked by unclear priorities on a Platform bug. Tried time-blocking (2 x 90m) but still fragmented.
Week 2 (11/10): instituted "no meeting mornings" on Tue/Thu. Saw +0.2 merged PRs, but review queue still long.
Week 3 (11/17): experiment: batch reviews into a single 60–90m slot. Reduced context switching, review turnaround improved to ~30h.
Week 4 (11/24): wrote draft doc: "lightweight rollout checklist" — got feedback from Nora. Mentorship slot added on Wednesdays.
Week 5 (12/01): slip week — travel + holiday. Metrics noisy. Learned that resilience rule needed for holidays (60% target).
Week 6 (12/08): re-focused on deep work: 2x90m blocks + strict Slack status. Mentorship minutes jumped; created a quick "how I review" guide for new hires.
Week 7 (12/15): consolidation and reflection. Merged PRs average ~1.3/week, review turnaround ~26h, docs authored 0.5/wk, mentorship ~55 min/wk. Close enough to target for a first pass.

Retrospective notes (wins / losses / surprises):
Wins:
- Time-blocking + single review batch captured the biggest lift. It reduced switching costs more than I expected.
- Quick docs (1–2 page) scaled: small effort, big reuse.
- Explicit mentorship slot made outreach more likely; fewer ad-hoc sessions.

Losses / what didn't work:
- Over-optimistic baseline for deep focus hours — meetings creep in. Need stronger boundary enforcement.
- Holiday week exposed fragility in metric approach.
- Occasionally swapped deep work for low-value async ops (responding to noise).

Surprises / learnings:
- Mentoring as a ritual not only helps others but surfaces small docs and refactors that reduce future review load.
- A single 90m review block is better than 4x15m scattered blocks.

Action items & experiments for next cycle:
1) Ritualize a weekly "review triage" (20m) + "deep review block" (90m) twice a week. (TODO: block recurring invites).
2) Experiment: 3-week "doc sprint" where I convert one recurring question into a public doc each week. Measure downstream reduction in review/context questions.
3) Build a tiny checklist template for PRs to reduce iteration (copy into template library).
4) Stronger meeting guardrails: add a GCal note and a quick Slack bot snippet to decline non-essential invites during blocked hours.
5) Track "noise time" weekly (time spent on reactive Slack/email) as a new metric.

Risks & blockers:
- Team context shifts (priority pivots) can invalidate a 7-week plan. Keep alignment checks with manager (quick 1:1 every other week).
- Personal calendar volatility (travel, health) — account for a 40% buffer in ambitious plans.

Notes to self (frank style):
- Be gentler on measurement: this is a learning sprint, not an engineering review.
- When a metric slips, jot 2 quick reasons and move on; avoid overfitting.
- Keep docs short and actionable. People appreciate checklists more than essays.

Quick wins for the coming week:
- Draft PR checklist (15–30m).
- Set recurring "deep review" blocks in calendar.
- Publish the first doc in "doc sprint" as a disposable draft and solicit feedback.

Open questions (to resolve in 1:1):
- Is the "effective contribution" formula reasonable for performance conversations? Should I track separate signals for mentorship vs. product output?
- Is the review batching compatible with team SLAs? (If not, adapt cadence).

Micro-tasks (one-liners):
- [ ] Create PR checklist template (due Fri).
- [ ] Set recurring deep-review blocks (Mon/Wed 10:00-11:30).
- [ ] Publish doc 1 (how I review) to team space and link in PRs.
- [ ] Add "noise time" counter to weekly snapshot.

Random friction notes (for later):
- Slack threading etiquette: remind folks to thread review requests.
- Consider a tiny bot to add PR checklists automatically if possible (file an RFC?).

Summary (one-liner):
Small structural changes (review batching + explicit mentoring slot + short docs) moved the needle; next cycle is about stabilizing rituals and reducing noise rather than another big push.

---
Revision history:
- 2025-11-02: created initial plan + metrics baseline.
- 2025-11-17: added weekly logs and early wins.
- 2026-03-05: cleaned up retrospective and added follow-up experiments.

Notes: keep this doc alive, fold into quarterly prep if I keep repeating the same experiments.
